02 · Set tests

fry for significance, singscore for where each sample sits

01_Gene_Sets ranks proteins and asks fgsea whether a set clusters at one end. That test treats the ranked proteins as exchangeable, and it calls sets significant on a contrast that cannot contain signal. This stage runs the two tests that do read the design.

fry() asks whether a set moved, using the participant design and limpa’s precision weights. It is a rotation test, so correlated members do not inflate it. singscore asks where each sample sits on each set, which is the number you can plot against the ultrasound measurements. Neither replaces the other: one gives a p-value, the other gives 131 numbers per set.

Does fry need a block term

01_Design put participant in the design as a fixed term, so every contrast is already tested within one person. What survives that is the correlation between the two samples of the same leg, and fry() would take it through block and correlation.

Measured on the matrix fry is about to test, not carried across from anywhere else. A correlation belongs to the matrix it was estimated on: this project once handed fry the singscore consensus of 0.29 instead of the protein-level 0.24, and 29 sets crossed the FDR line on the strength of it.

leg_id <- paste(proteins$targets$participant, proteins$targets$leg, sep = "_")
rho <- duplicateCorrelation(proteins$E, d$design, block = leg_id)$consensus.correlation
round(c(within_leg_correlation = rho), 4)
within_leg_correlation 
                0.0272

Near zero, as it was at the design stage, so fry() runs without block. If this ever rose, the fix is to pass block = leg_id, correlation = rho below — but read the number first, because nothing here branches on it.

fry

One call per contrast: fry() takes a single contrast vector, not a matrix. It reads fit$EList$weights, which is what limpa’s per-observation standard errors became, so a protein reconstructed largely from missing precursors counts for less here too.

fry_results <- run_fry_all(
  proteins$E, set_indices, d$design, d$contrasts,
  weights = fit$EList$weights
) |>
  mutate(collection = params$collection, .before = 1)

fry_results |>
  summarise(
    tested = n(),
    up = sum(FDR < params$set_fdr & Direction == "Up"),
    down = sum(FDR < params$set_fdr & Direction == "Down"),
    min_fdr = signif(min(FDR), 3), .by = contrast
  )
contrast tested up down min_fdr

BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T1 1032 0 0 1.00e+00
BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T2 1032 0 0 5.01e-01

The negative control

BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T1 compares two legs of one person before either was trained. A set test that respects the design should find nothing here. fgsea did not; this is the comparison that matters.

fry_results |>
  filter(contrast == d$negative_control) |>
  slice_min(PValue, n = 5) |>
  select(set_id, NGenes, Direction, PValue, FDR)

Where each sample sits

singscore ranks each sample’s proteins and scores every set against those ranks, giving one number per set per sample. It carries no p-value and no design; simpleScore() returns a score and a dispersion, and the permutation route in generateNull() handles one set per call at a thousand re-scorings each, answering a per-sample question that never sees the contrast. The scores are the useful output, and fry above supplies the significance.

scores <- score_samples(proteins$E, pathway$protein_map, sets)
dim(scores)
[1] 1032  131

Set-level scores are a different matrix from the protein one, so their intra-block correlation is a different number and belongs only to fits run on them. It is recorded here and used nowhere else in this notebook.

rho_sets <- duplicateCorrelation(scores, d$design, block = leg_id)$consensus.correlation
round(c(set_score_correlation = rho_sets, protein_correlation = rho), 4)
set_score_correlation   protein_correlation 
               0.0455                0.0272

Scores against the phenotype

phenotype.csv is one row per leg, which is why it is joined on participant and leg rather than on sample. Each leg contributes two samples, so the change in a set’s score across the two timepoints is what pairs with a change in cross-sectional area.

score_change <- scores |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("set_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-set_id, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "score") |>
  left_join(proteins$targets, by = "sample_id") |>
  select(set_id, participant, leg, timepoint, score) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = score) |>
  mutate(score_change = T2 - T1) |>
  inner_join(inputs$phenotype, by = c("participant", "leg")) |>
  mutate(csa_change = vl_csa_post_cm2 - vl_csa_pre_cm2)

# Every set against the same outcome, so the ranking is the point, not any single p-value.
csa_correlation <- score_change |>
  filter(!is.na(csa_change), !is.na(score_change)) |>
  summarise(
    legs = n(),
    r = cor(score_change, csa_change, method = "spearman"), .by = set_id
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(r)))

slice_head(csa_correlation, n = 10)

No multiplicity correction is applied to that table and none is implied: it ranks sets by how their movement tracks hypertrophy, across 1032 sets, and any one row would need its own test.

A signature from one contrast, tested on another

Take the proteins that moved with high-load training, then ask whether restriction moved the same ones. Building the signature from HLRT_post_vs_pre and testing it on BFR_post_vs_pre keeps the two independent; building and testing on the same contrast would be circular and always significant.

The same signature is tested on BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T1, where it must find nothing. Read that row before either of the others.

signature <- pathway$protein_results |>
  filter(
    contrast == "HLRT_post_vs_pre", selected, !is.na(gene),
    adj.P.Val < params$signature_fdr
  ) |>
  slice_min(adj.P.Val, n = params$signature_max) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(logFC > 0, "up", "down"))

signature_index <- signature |>
  split(~direction) |>
  map(\(part) match(part$protein, protein_ids))

c(up = length(signature_index$up), down = length(signature_index$down))
  up down 
  61   46 
map(set_names(c("BFR_post_vs_pre", d$negative_control, "interaction")), \(contrast) {
  fry(
    y = proteins$E, index = signature_index, design = d$design,
    contrast = d$contrasts[, contrast], weights = fit$EList$weights,
    sort = "none"
  ) |>
    rownames_to_column("direction")
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "tested_on") |>
  select(tested_on, direction, NGenes, Direction, PValue, FDR)
tested_on direction NGenes Direction PValue FDR
BFR_post_vs_pre down 46 Down 0.0000000 0.0000000
BFR_post_vs_pre up 61 Up 0.0000000 0.0000000
BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T1 down 46 Down 0.2227772 0.2227772
BFR_vs_HLRT_at_T1 up 61 Up 0.0301742 0.0603484
interaction down 46 Up 0.0511890 0.0511890
interaction up 61 Down 0.0150949 0.0301898

Measured here, the control does not come back empty: the up half returns p = 0.030 on two untrained legs of one person. It stays above FDR 0.05, but only just, and the adjustment runs over two tests. A signature selected for large effects may simply be selecting the proteins with the widest baseline spread between legs, which no amount of cross-contrast testing fixes. The interaction row below rests on that control and should not be read as a result.

The fixed sets above do not share the problem, since they were defined before any contrast was seen, and fry returns nothing on the control across all of them.

Every sample also gets a score on that signature, up and down together, so the response can be plotted per participant rather than read only as a p-value.

gene_map <- filter(pathway$protein_map, selected)
signature_matrix <- proteins$E[gene_map$protein, ]
rownames(signature_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
signature_score <- singscore::simpleScore(
  singscore::rankGenes(signature_matrix),
  upSet = signature$gene[signature$direction == "up"],
  downSet = signature$gene[signature$direction == "down"]
) |>
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  left_join(proteins$targets, by = "sample_id")

ggplot(signature_score, aes(timepoint, TotalScore, group = participant)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "high-load signature score",
    caption = "signature defined on HLRT_post_vs_pre; each line is one participant's leg"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

      "fry run without block: participant is fixed in the design and the",
      "residual within-leg correlation is near zero"
    ),
    signature = "Defined on HLRT_post_vs_pre, tested on BFR_post_vs_pre and the negative control"
  )
)
